assessments.rationale: Both annotations agree the dominant signal is a coherent primary-cilia biogenesis/trafficking module built on the same gene set, situated in postnatal brain endothelium. Beyond that shared core, the two diverge substantively: the candidate replaces the baseline's mechanosensory/shear-stress interpretation of ciliary function with a Hedgehog-signaling (Smo/GPR161 trafficking) interpretation, introduces an unrelated mitochondrial mechanism absent from the baseline, and drops the baseline's regulatory narrative built on Gata2, Eng, and Tet1 (BBB maintenance, TGF-β vascular remodeling, epigenetic angiogenic control), retaining only Fzd4. These are not just added detail or citations — they change what the program is claimed to functionally do (mechanotransduction vs. Hedgehog signaling) and what regulatory genes are implicated in its identity/BBB role, which could lead a reader to prioritize different validation experiments or follow-up hypotheses. This crosses from refinement into material reinterpretation.

assessments.rationale: Both annotations agree on the central claim: P10 is a primary-cilia/ciliopathy gene program operating in postnatal brain endothelial cells, with Fzd4/Gata2/Eng regulators framing endothelial identity. The candidate retains this core but adds a genuinely new submechanism (mitochondrial metabolism, supported by a disjoint gene set) and reframes the cilia mechanism toward disease-syndrome annotation rather than the specific mechanosensory/BBB-genesis functional model baseline offered, while also compressing the regulator mechanism into a much thinner treatment. Per the rubric, 'adds a meaningful submechanism' and 'removes/weakens a prior conclusion' are the defining features of same_core_with_meaningful_refinement rather than materially_changed — no existing mechanism is contradicted or reversed, but real gains and losses in mechanistic detail occur across mitochondrial biology (added), endothelial mechanosensing (lost), and vascular regulatory signaling (weakened).

assessments.rationale: Both annotations converge on the same central biological story: P21 is the hepatic de novo cholesterol biosynthesis pathway under SCAP/INSIG1-SREBP2 transcriptional control, balanced against Ldlr-mediated uptake, fed by Acss2-derived acetyl-CoA, and coupled to Dgat2/Mttp-driven VLDL-TG export in the MASLD context. No mechanism, direction, or regulatory relationship is reversed or contradicted. The candidate's value-add is (1) a new gene-function claim (Rdh11 as an SREBP2 target), (2) a specific mechanistic role for Erg28 that was previously just a listed gene, (3) explicit acknowledgment of unexplained distinctive genes, and (4) denser gene-specific and context-specific literature support (KO phenotypes, Acss2/Acly relationship, Mttp-Acat2 interaction, quantitative Scap effect size). These are meaningful refinements and gene-function assignments layered onto an unchanged core interpretation, not a change in the program's biological identity or the direction of any regulatory effect.

assessments.rationale: Both annotations agree P21 is the mevalonate-to-cholesterol biosynthesis program under SCAP/Insig1/SREBP2 control with the same enzyme roster and the same MASLD-linked regulators (Dgat2, Mttp) — the central interpretation is preserved. The candidate meaningfully refines this with gene-specific mechanistic claims (Erg28 as scaffold with feedback to SREBP2, direct SRE sites for three genes) and extends the MASLD arm with a new gene (Ddr2) and regulator (Fads2). It also drops two baseline claims (Ldlr as uptake arm; senescence/ERRα/mitochondrial link in aging) without replacing them with an aging-relevant mechanism, which is a real narrowing of the disease-context narrative but does not alter the program's core enzymatic/regulatory identity. This pattern — retained core, added gene-function detail, one context-level mechanism reframed/removed — matches 'same_core_with_meaningful_refinement' rather than a material change to the program's central interpretation.

assessments.rationale: Both annotations agree on two of three core themes: a pericentral Phase I/II detox battery and a lipid-droplet/peroxisomal fatty-acid-oxidation program, with the candidate adding gene-specific mechanistic detail (Htatip2, EET synthesis, PPARalpha regulation of Sult2a8) that refines rather than changes these two themes. However, baseline's third mechanism — sulfur amino acid catabolism feeding hepatic nitrogen/ammonia disposal via the urea cycle, built on Cdo1+Car5a+Agmat — is absent from the candidate. Car5a and Agmat disappear entirely, and Cdo1 is reassigned into a new bile-acid-taurine-conjugation mechanism instead. This is not merely added detail or a qualifier on an existing conclusion; it is the loss of one of three central program mechanisms and a re-attribution of a shared gene's function, which would lead a reader to a different conclusion about what the program does biologically (nitrogen/ammonia handling vs. bile acid conjugation only). That crosses into materially_changed rather than refinement.

assessments.rationale: Both annotations converge on the same three-theme architecture (Phase II bile acid/steroid sulfation, peroxisomal fatty acid oxidation/lipid droplet handling, sulfur/nitrogen catabolism with an aging signature) and rely on largely overlapping gene sets and regulators, so the core biological identity of P25 is unchanged. However, the candidate drops the baseline's explicit Nrf2/CAR transcriptional-regulation narrative and the Cyp2c50 phase I enzyme, swaps Eci2/Lonp2 for a new Psmd1 proteasome-lipogenesis mechanism, and replaces the cited Cdo1-gluconeogenesis link with a CoA-synthesis claim. These are meaningful gene-function and mechanistic refinements/losses rather than a wholesale reinterpretation, placing this at same_core_with_meaningful_refinement with mixed evidence depth change (gains in some gene-specific detail, losses in regulatory/mechanistic specificity elsewhere).
